title: London's Diwali on the Square Cancelled as Storm Boelo Makes Build Unsafe
excerpt: City Hall called off Sunday's Trafalgar Square celebration on safety advice, as 80mph gusts and heavy rain sweep the UK this weekend.
body:
• London's Diwali on the Square, due in Trafalgar Square on Sunday, October 25 from 1pm to 7pm, has been cancelled on the advice of independent health and safety experts.
  • The Mayor of London's office said storms forecast for Saturday made it unsafe to build and set up the event; Storm Boelo is bringing gusts of up to 80mph to parts of the UK.
  • The free event was to open with 200 dancers and feature music, dance, food stalls and family activities for London's Hindu, Sikh and Jain communities.
  • If you planned to travel in, do not go to Trafalgar Square on Sunday — City Hall says it is considering other ways to support Diwali celebrations in London this year.

London's Diwali on the Square celebrations, scheduled for Trafalgar Square on Sunday, October 25, have been cancelled following the recommendation of independent event health and safety experts, the Mayor of London's office announced on Saturday.

With storms forecast on Saturday, the event's health and safety leads advised that it would not be safe to carry out the build and set-up required to stage the event on Sunday. The decision, City Hall said, was taken in line with that professional advice, with the safety of everyone involved the absolute priority, according to BizAsia's report of the statement.

"The safety of Londoners and visitors must come first."

— Mayor of London's office, cancellation statement

A storm weekend across Britain

The cancellation comes as Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, follows Storm Austen across the UK this weekend. The Met Office expects the strongest winds across Northern Ireland, northern England and Scotland, with gusts of up to 80mph in exposed areas, heavy rain, possible flooding and a risk of power cuts. Forecasters say rainfall could exceed 100mm in a day on higher ground in Scotland.

https://x.com/Londonist/status/2113965403076477209

Trafalgar Square itself sits outside the worst of the wind warnings, but the staging for a major open-air event — scaffolding, lighting rigs and temporary structures — has to go up the day before, in the middle of Saturday's storm. That build window is what the safety experts judged unsafe.

What has been lost

Diwali on the Square is one of the largest public Diwali celebrations outside India. When Mayor Sadiq Khan announced this year's edition on the City Hall website, the free, family-friendly event was set to run from 1pm to 7pm, opening with a dance sequence performed by 200 dancers, followed by music and dance celebrating the heritage of London's Hindu, Sikh and Jain communities. Around the Square there were to be arts and crafts, storytelling, yoga and meditation, dance workshops, a Ramayana puppet show for families, and food stalls serving vegan and vegetarian cuisine.

The event is delivered with the volunteer-led Diwali in London committee. City Hall acknowledged the disappointment for attendees and for volunteers who had spent months preparing, and said it had not taken the decision lightly.

What happens next

The Mayor's office said it is now considering other ways to support people to celebrate Diwali in London this year, but announced no replacement date or venue on Saturday. Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8 in 2026, and London's temples and community organisations run their own celebrations through the festival period — those indoor events are not affected by this cancellation.

For the diaspora in London, the practical advice is simple: Sunday's Trafalgar Square event will not happen, travel and weather disruption is expected across much of the UK through the weekend, and anyone with outdoor plans should check Met Office warnings before setting out.
